## Re-scoped to Path 2 (harvest-worktree auto-recovery)

Path 1b (stop injecting ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT) shipped in commit 1e736d4a3b as cleanup — it removes the deliberate-pointer surface but does NOT close the underlying breach. Empirical diagnostic (agent aafe) confirmed three independent leak surfaces remain even after Path 1b:

- git worktree list — structural to git, enumerates all worktrees
- Filesystem read access — same user, same FS
- Filesystem write access — no OS-level fence

So Path 1b alone is not a fix for this ticket. The complementary work needed:

### This ticket = Path 2 (harvest-side transparent recovery)

Re-scope: extend harvest-worktree.sh (or sprint Phase F) to detect commits in the session worktree whose DSO-Story: / DSO-Story-Merge: trailers name a branch different from the current branch, automatically cherry-pick them onto the named target branch, emit a structured log entry, and continue. Transparent to the user — no prompt, no halt.

### Overlapping scope assigned to epic b36c-3e66-c0f2-413d

Epic b36c-3e66 (horn-womb-corgi: 'Make forbidden-action HARD-GATEs in brainstorm/sprint/fix-bug/implementation-plan load-bearing via tool-use-time enforcement') is assigned the agent-layer side: every implementer-class agent file (~28 files) gets explicit guidance to derive write paths exclusively from its own CWD and never enumerate sibling worktrees. That work eliminates the AGENT-side temptation to construct session-worktree paths.

The two work streams complement each other:
- b36c (agent layer): prevents the breach at source
- This ticket / Path 2 (harvest layer): recovers gracefully if a breach happens anyway

9679 closes when Path 2 lands; b36c proceeds independently per its own scope and timing.
